title: surveyreports Package Development
text: govern every implementation decision. doubt, use tiebreaker. DRY — flag repetition aggressively. Repeated logic 2+ functions → extract shared helper. Repeated validation → consolidate. Repeated test setup → move helper-*.R. Surface DRY violations spec review, . Well-tested — tests better. 98%+ line coverage floor. Every error class gets test. Every edge case spec gets test. Never suggest removing coverage hit deadline. Engineered enough — , . -engineered: missing edge cases, happy-path-validation. -engineered: abstraction without two real call sites, generalization hypothetical future work. Right-size current spec. Handle edge cases, fewer. -NA inputs, zero-weight rows, single-level groups, empty domains — appear real survey data. Thoughtfulness > speed. Explicit clever. S7::S7_inherits(x, ClassName) inherits(x, "string"). Named error classes every cli_abort(). Spell behavior specs rather leaving implicit.

what: ANES 2024: American National Election Studies Time Series — anes_2024
title: ANES 2024: American National Election Studies Time Series — anes_2024
text: 19-variable extract 2024 American National Election Studies (ANES) Time Series Study, landmark biennial pre- post-election survey American electorate. Fielded via face--face interview web (n = 5,521). extract uses FTF + Web combined design variables (v240103a–v240103d), recommended set analyses.

title: ANES 2024: American National Election Studies Time Series — anes_2024
code: anes_2024

title: ANES 2024: American National Election Studies Time Series — anes_2024
text: data frame 5,521 rows 19 variables: v240103a Pre-election weight (FTF+Web combined). Use variables asked November 5, 2024. v240103b Post-election weight (FTF+Web combined). Use variables asked November 5, 2024. v240103c PSU (FTF+Web combined). Use cluster ID variance estimation. v240103d Stratum (FTF+Web combined). Use stratification variable. v240001 2024 Time Series Case ID. Unique respondent identifier. v240003 Sample type: 1 = Panel, 2 = Fresh Web, 3 = Fresh FTF, 4 = GSS. v240002c Pre/Post interview completion: 1 = Pre-election , 2 = Pre- post-election. v243002 State FIPS code. v243007 Census region: 1 = Northeast, 2 = Midwest, 3 = South, 4 = West. v241458x Age Election Day (summary). Top-coded 80. -2 = missing. v241550 Sex: 1 = male, 2 = female. v241501x Race/ethnicity (5-category summary): White non-Hispanic, Black non-Hispanic, Hispanic, Asian/NHPI non-Hispanic, /Multiracial non-Hispanic. v241465x Education (5-category summary): 1 = less HS, 2 = HS diploma, 3 = college, 4 = bachelor's degree, 5 = graduate degree. v241566x Household income (28 categories < $5,000 $250,000+). v241177 Liberal-conservative self-placement (7-point scale): 1 = extremely liberal, 7 = extremely conservative. 99 = thought . v241222 Party identification strength: 1 = strong, 2 = strong. v241223 Party identification lean (Independents): 1 = closer Republican, 2 = neither, 3 = closer Democrat. v242066 respondent vote President (POST): 1 = yes, 2 = . v242067 Presidential vote choice (POST): 1 = Harris, 2 = Trump, 3 = RFK Jr., 4 = West, 5 = Stein, 6 = .

title: ANES 2024: American National Election Studies Time Series — anes_2024
text: American National Election Studies. 2024 Time Series Study. Available electionstudies.org (free account required download raw data; processed .rda included package). Prepared data-raw/prepare-anes-2024.R.

title: ANES 2024: American National Election Studies Time Series — anes_2024
text: Survey design: Stratified cluster — use Taylor series linearization. Two weights available depending whether analysis uses pre- post-election variables:   Missing value codes: ANES uses negative integer codes missing data throughout: -9 = Refused, -8 = know, -4 = Technical error, -1 = Inapplicable, others. must recoded NA analysis. Check attr(anes_2024$v241177, "labels") full set codes given variable. Metadata: columns carry variable labels value labels R attributes original Stata file, automatically extracted surveycore's metadata system call surveycore::as_survey(). Variable labels ("label" attribute): human-readable description column. Example: attr(anes_2024$v241550, "label") returns "PRE: sex?" (similar ANES phrasing). Value labels ("labels" attribute): named numeric vector mapping code meaning, including missing-value codes. Example: attr(anes_2024$v241550, "labels") returns vector entries Male, Female, applicable negative missing codes.
code: # Pre-election analysis (party ID, ideology, candidate preference) svy_pre <- surveycore::as_survey(anes_2024,   ids     = v240103c,   strata  = v240103d,   weights = v240103a,   nest    = TRUE )  # Post-election analysis (validated vote choice) svy_post <- surveycore::as_survey(anes_2024,   ids     = v240103c,   strata  = v240103d,   weights = v240103b,   nest    = TRUE )

title: GSS 2024: General Social Survey — gss_2024
text: 27-variable extract 2024 General Social Survey (GSS), one longest-running sociological surveys United States (fielded annually biennially since 1972). 3,309 respondents 2024 cross-section included.

title: GSS 2024: General Social Survey — gss_2024
text: data frame 3,309 rows 27 variables: vpsu Variance primary sampling unit. Use cluster ID variance estimation. vstrat Variance stratum. Use stratification variable. wtssps Person post-stratification weight. Standard analysis weight. wtssnrps Person post-stratification weight adjusted differential non-response. Preferred non-response bias concern. id Respondent ID. Unique case identifier. year Survey year (2024 extract). ballot Ballot form (, B, C, D). GSS uses split-ballot design; questions appear every ballot. Inapplicable items coded -100. age Age years (89 = 89 older). sex Sex: 1 = male, 2 = female. race Race: 1 = white, 2 = black, 3 = . hispanic Hispanic origin: 1 = Hispanic; 2–50 = specific Hispanic origin. educ Highest year school completed (0–20 years). degree Highest degree: 0 = less HS, 1 = high school, 2 = associate, 3 = bachelor's, 4 = graduate. income16 Total family income (26 categories < $1,000 $170,000+). marital Marital status: 1 = married, 2 = widowed, 3 = divorced, 4 = separated, 5 = never married. wrkstat Labor force status: 1 = full time, 2 = part time, 3 = temporarily working, 4 = unemployed, 5 = retired, 6 = school, 7 = keeping house, 8 = . hrs1 Hours worked last week (employed respondents ). adults Number adults household (8 = 8 ). partyid Party identification: 0 = strong Democrat, 3 = Independent, 6 = strong Republican, 7 = party. polviews Political views: 1 = extremely liberal, 7 = extremely conservative. happy General happiness: 1 = happy, 2 = pretty happy, 3 = happy. health Self-rated health: 1 = excellent, 2 = good, 3 = fair, 4 = poor. trust Social trust: 1 = people can trusted, 2 = careful, 3 = depends. natfare Government spending welfare: 1 = little, 2 = right, 3 = much. abany Abortion reason: 1 = yes, 2 = . attend Religious service attendance: 0 = never, 8 = several times week. relig Religious preference: 1 = Protestant, 2 = Catholic, 3 = Jewish, 4 = none, others.

title: GSS 2024: General Social Survey — gss_2024
text: NORC University Chicago. General Social Survey 2024. https://gss.norc.org (free account required download raw data; processed .rda included package). Prepared data-raw/prepare-gss-2024.R.

title: GSS 2024: General Social Survey — gss_2024
text: Survey design: Stratified multi-stage cluster — use Taylor series linearization:   Missing value codes: GSS uses consistent system negative integer codes missing data across variables: codes stored value labels every column (check attr(gss_2024$happy, "labels")). Recode NA analysis. Split-ballot design: ballot variable indicates question module respondent received. Variables asked ballots -100 (Inapplicable) respondents ballots. Metadata: columns carry variable labels value labels R attributes original SPSS file, automatically extracted surveycore's metadata system call surveycore::as_survey(). Variable labels ("label" attribute): human-readable description column. Example: attr(gss_2024$happy, "label") returns "GENERAL HAPPINESS". Value labels ("labels" attribute): named numeric vector mapping code meaning, including missing-value codes. Example: attr(gss_2024$happy, "labels") returns entries happy, Pretty happy, happy, negative missing codes.

Value labels ("labels" attribute): named numeric vector mapping code meaning. Example: attr(pew_jewish_2020$relconsider_a, "labels") returns c("Yes, Consider " = 1, ", Consider " = 2, Refused = 99). Question preface ("question_preface" attribute): shared question stem battery group. text: results list (named unnamed) tibbles / data frames. Every element must contain column named per p_col. Length must least one. List elements may heterogeneous column sets; missing columns NA-filled bind. method Character(1). Adjustment method, passed verbatim stats::p.adjust(). One stats::p.adjust.methods. Default "BH". p_col Character(1). Name column holding raw p-values pooled. Default "p_value". Must exist every list element. new_col Character(1). Name column pooled- adjusted p-values written. Default "p_value_adj". id_col Character(1). Name source-identifier column added bound output. Default "source". Filled list names; unnamed elements integer index coerced character (matching dplyr::bind_rows(.id = ...) semantics). strip_within_adj Logical(1). FALSE (default) input contains column named per new_col, column renamed paste0(new_col, "_within") per element binding, warning emitted. TRUE, pre-existing new_col column silently dropped element binding; warning.

Column ordering: (1) union input columns input-union order; (2) id_col; (3) new_col; (4) paste0(new_col, "_within") applicable. result carries .meta attribute (list) keys method, family_size, n_total, n_na, n_significant_05, id_col, p_col, new_col.

title: Pool p-values across a list of analysis results and apply a single family-wise multiplicity correction — pool_pvals
text: pool_pvals() dispatches verbatim stats::p.adjust(); adjustment formula determined entirely method. "BH" (Benjamini-Hochberg, 1995) – controls false discovery rate (FDR) independence positive regression dependency (PRDS). Recommended default multi-DV survey families. "" (Benjamini-Yekutieli, 2001) – controls FDR arbitrary dependence; strictly conservative BH. Use dependence structure across DVs unknown arbitrary. "fdr" – alias "BH" per stats::p.adjust() source. two identical. "holm" (Holm, 1979) – controls family-wise error rate (FWER) arbitrary dependence. Uniformly powerful Bonferroni. "hochberg" (Hochberg, 1988) – controls FWER, requires independence MTP_2 dependence (just PRDS). Use Holm instead DVs correlated FWER control desired. "hommel" (Hommel, 1988) – controls FWER, requires independence MTP_2 dependence. caveat Hochberg. "bonferroni" – controls FWER dependence structure (Bonferroni's inequality). conservative FWER procedures; preferred tiny families. "none" – pass-; raw p-values returned new_col.

title: Pool p-values across a list of analysis results and apply a single family-wise multiplicity correction — pool_pvals
text: default method = "BH" reflects typical structure survey p-values across DVs, usually positively dependent (PRDS) rarely independent. dependence structure unknown known arbitrary, switch method = "" robust FDR-controlling alternative.
